subject: Remote unseal & rotation plan for on-prem BYOK deployment

Subject: On-prem BYOK: unseal/rotation expectations and evidence request

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare the procurement checklist for our private deployment, Security has two important asks we want to lock in before sign-off:

1) Detailed unseal procedure for HSM-backed keys when our cluster is rebooted or when an operator performs maintenance (we need who/what/where).
2) Evidence we can provide auditors that a rotation completed successfully (audit logs, signed attestations).

We understand Redwood supports BYOK with HSM import and can do split-key escrow, but we need a concrete runbook that matches our control plane-on-prem split model and that fits within our maintenance windows (Saturdays 02:00–05:00 UTC). Can you share the proposed operator separation pattern and what evidence we can collect without exposing key material?

Attaching a high-level diagram of our network zones and the questions in-line in the PDF.

Appreciate a plan and whether Redwood recommends a dry-run cadence before go-live.

—Alex
Director, Infrastructure Security
FinServCo

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: On-prem BYOK: unseal/rotation expectations and evidence request

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram. I pulled together a draft runbook and attached a short playbook (rotation-runbook.md) plus a proposed unseal operator flow. High level answers up front:

- Unseal model: quorum-based remote unseal using operator-held key shares (Shamir), with the Redwood on-prem agent only able to call the HSM through a bastion jump and a short-lived service account token (no persistent key in the control plane).
- Operator separation: at least 3 distinct operator keys required for unseal; no single operator can both trigger the request and supply all shares. We recommend one operator from FinServCo, one from your ops/vendor team, and one from a Redwood operator for the initial handoff period.
- Evidence: HSM logs + signed unseal attestations (RFC3161 timestamped) and a rotation manifest that lists previous key id, new key id (key id hashes only), who initiated, and a link to the KMS audit stream. We provide a signed JSON attestation (not the raw key material).

Notes/constraints:
- Time-to-unseal: expect 60–120s for the live path if your network-bastion is healthy. Air-gapped sites will require courier-assisted share transfer (we outline an encrypted USB + signed manifest procedure).
- Rotation window: we recommend scheduled rewrap + HSM rekey during your maintenance window; the runbook includes a fallback plan that uses dual-key serving (old & new) to avoid rollback risk.

I put Karthis and Marissa on copy to cover the HSM operator steps and audit evidence. We propose a dry-run next Tuesday (UTC) where we simulate the unseal and collect the attestation output.

Will schedule a 30m run-through with your team if that works.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: On-prem BYOK: unseal/rotation expectations and evidence request

Alex/Tessa — quick technical follow-up and some implementation clarifications.

1) HSM model and key provenance: we will import your wrapped key material into the HSM using a customer-keystore import workflow (BYOK). The HSM only stores the wrapped blob; the import operation generates a key_handle bound to module firmware. The runbook includes the exact CLI/API calls and a code sample for the import flow.

2) Remote unseal options: three supported modes in our private package:
  - Network unseal: operator connects to bastion -> invokes unseal API -> HSM requires 3/5 shares (quorum). This is the standard flow for connected sites.
  - Courier unseal: operator prints signed manifest, transfers shares offline on FIPS-validated USB, performs local unseal with offline HSM operator. Useful for air-gapped sites.
  - Automated threshold HSM (advanced): HSM internal thresholding using operator tokens + HSM-second-factor (requires vendor firmware feature).

3) Rotation and rewrap: we do rolling rewraps at application layer so tokens issued remain valid for ttl; rewrap is HSM-mediated and we publish rotation manifests to your audit collector (syslog/S3 with retention policy). The manifest contains only key fingerprints and signed attestations.

4) Evidence for auditors: we provide a hashed chain-of-custody (SHA256 entries) linking the import event, rotation events, and the attestation signatures. We also recommend you retain the audit stream for 7 years per your policy; we can forward to a customer-managed S3 or SIEM.

Action items captured in the runbook:

- T: confirm operator list and access method (network vs courier) — owner: Alex
- T: provide SOC2 evidence spec (what logs are required by your auditor) — owner: FinServCo

I'll be on the call to walk through the CLI steps.

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of clarifications before the dry-run: 

- For the dry-run please simulate both the network unseal and the courier unseal. We will have an on-call ops engineer for the latter.
- On evidence: our auditor requires a signed timestamp with the attestation (RFC3161 is fine) and a manifest that can be verified independently using a public key. Can Redwood provide the verification key for the attestation signatures?
- Can you also confirm whether the signed attestation will include the operator identity (email/uid) or only an operator key fingerprint? Our compliance prefers an identity claim (we recognize legal constraints and are okay if Redwood provides hashed identities).

If you can share the dry-run calendar invite and the pre-call checklist (including the commands you will run and the expected output) that would help speed sign-off.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
Director, Infrastructure Security, FinServCo
